archetypes.name: oos-pipeline
archetypes.rationale: The diff changes a multi-script artifact pipeline where accepted OOS blocks can be dropped, duplicated, or overwritten across tally, emit, and review-and-fix paths.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace accepted non-security OOS data flow across tally-code-votes.sh, emit-tally.sh, review-and-fix.sh, and the disposition counters. Look for cases where normalized blocks are not written, are written twice, are overwritten later, or fail to mirror into the implement tmpdir. Pay special attention to OOS_ACCEPTED_COUNT, OOS_ACCEPTED_FILE versus OOS_ACCEPTED_OUT, missing oos.md, and multi-round accumulated-oos.md behavior. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: shell-portability
archetypes.rationale: The patch adds shell and awk helper logic that must remain Bash 3.2 and BSD-compatible while behaving correctly under set -euo pipefail.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect the new normalize-oos-block-header.sh helper and its call sites for Bash 3.2 portability, quoting, stdin versus file behavior, awk portability, and set -e interactions. Check whether command substitutions preserve the intended block contents and whether argument validation handles edge cases without surprising callers. Also verify that added test code does not rely on GNU-only behavior. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: counter-parity
archetypes.rationale: The reader backstop is implemented in both Python and awk, so semantic drift could cause different disposition outcomes in separate gates.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare the legacy-header counting rules in python/oos.py and skills/implement/scripts/oos-non-security-block-count.awk. Verify they agree on tagged FINDING headers, bare FINDING headers, canonical OOS headers, block boundaries, and security focus-area exclusions. Look for regex differences that could produce divergent non-security counts or false positives. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-coverage
archetypes.rationale: The plan relies heavily on regression harnesses to prove narrow pipeline behavior, and gaps could leave #3550 partially unfixed.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the added and modified tests for whether they actually exercise the production paths claimed in the plan. Check that new Makefile targets are wired into the intended shard, fixtures cover both preserve and fallback branches, and assertions would fail for the original bug. Identify any brittle assertions, missing negative cases, or tests that pass despite the implementation not satisfying the contract. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
